newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe, S.Africa in political and trade talks.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe, S.Africa in political and trade talks.

text.p: Zimbabwe and South Africa started two days of talks on Monday aimed at boosting trade and political relations strained over the years by charges that Pretoria is using its stronger economy to dominate its northern neighbour.

Zimbabwean Deputy Foreign Minister Nicholas Goche opened the inaugural meeting of the Zimbabwe-South Africa Joint Commission playing down the anger regularly voiced by Zimbabwean business leaders, but he said South Africa should do more to improve ties and to reduce a growing trade imbalance.

South Africa is Zimbabwe's largest trading partner in Africa, but their relations have suffered over long drawn-out negotiations to renew a 1964 preferential trade pact. After that pact expired in 1992 Pretoria tripled tariffs on textile imports from Zimbabwe.

Pretoria agreed only three months ago to reduce the clothing and textile tariffs to their previous 30 percent rate following persistent accusations by Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe that South Africa was waging war on its neighbours, and threats that he would take retaliatory measures.

"I am encouraged by the fact that our ministries of trade and industry have gone a long way to define a way forward in resolving this issue," Goche said, calling for concrete cooperation and inviting South African companies to invest in Zimbabwe's planned export processing zones.

In a replay of regular accusations, Zimbabwe's Confederation of Industries (CZI) charged again at the weekend that South Africa paid only lip service to the need for closer bilateral and regional economic relations.
South African Deputy Foreign Minister Asmal Pahad, who is leading a 50-member delegation to the Harare talks, told the joint commission meeting on Monday his country meant what it said.

"South Africa fully recognises its responsibility in this regard...The fortunes of South Africa and Zimbabwe, and indeed those of the whole region, are dependent on our capacity to utilise opportunities that are presented to us," he said.

The recent signing of a trade protocol of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) -- made up of Angola, Botswana, Zambia, Zimbabwe, South Africa, Swaziland, Mauritius, Malawi, Namibia, Lesotho, Tanzania and Mozambique -- would help boost trade relations, he said.
Talks on a comprehensive trade agreement with Zimbabwe would be pursued at a meeting of trade ministers planned to take place in coming weeks, Pahad said.
